rowan: Elder Rowan: Ah! Our young chef! Word travels quickly in a village this small. Especially when delivered by a pigeon that refuses to leave my roof.
Elder Rowan: So the King needs a feast, does he? Then the royal kitchens have chosen well. Or chosen desperately. Time shall tell!
Elder Rowan: The ingredients you seek are no ordinary harvest. Each belongs to an old tale, and each tale hides a little truth.
Elder Rowan: In Riverwood, the Dewcrown grows where the river keeps the land apart. Bram the lumberjack knows those woods better than anyone.
Elder Rowan: In the Whispering Peaks, they say even stones can fly. Speak with Mira by the northern gate.
Elder Rowan: And the fires of Emberfall? Flint the blacksmith has been babbling about those furnaces for years. For once, it might be worth listening.
Elder Rowan: Remember this, chef: when the road seems impossible, look at what the world has placed around you.
Chef (thought): Look around, ask questions, and try not to burn dinner. Understood.
rowan_repeat: Elder Rowan: An old story is only useful if you remember to look for the truth inside it.
Elder Rowan: Your royal letter should remind you which ingredients remain.
bram: Bram: Hold it there. You don't look like a woodcutter.
Bram: A chef? In these woods? Hah! I suppose even mushrooms have become difficult to find these days.
Bram: You're after the Dewcrown, aren't you? Aye, I've seen it. Glows like moonlight, tastes like heaven, and grows on the wrong side of the river.
Bram: Trouble is, the river's too deep to wade. And there's no bridge left standing around here.
Bram: My grandfather used to say, "When the forest won't give you a path, ask the trees."
Bram: There's an old oak by the water. Trunk's been weak for years. I've always wondered which way it'd fall.
Chef (thought): Ask the trees? I wonder if my spatula is sturdy enough.
bram_repeat: Bram: That big oak by the river has seen better days.
Bram: A good whack can work wonders. Just don't stand where it falls!
mira: Mira: Off to the mountains, are you? Splendid! Most people prefer to admire them from a comfortable distance.
Mira: The Skyfeather Bird nests beyond the Whispering Chasm. No ordinary person can jump that far.
Mira: But something curious happens up there. I've watched pebbles rise from the valley instead of falling into it.
Mira: The old mountaineers called them the Breath of the Mountains. Invisible winds strong enough to carry almost anything.
Mira: If you want my advice, bring something you can throw. It's better to lose a stone than find out what happens when you jump blindly.
Chef (thought): Invisible wind... Perhaps I can find a way across.
mira_repeat: Mira: If you can't see a path, look for how the world reacts to it.
Mira: The mountains leave clues for those patient enough to notice.
flint: Flint: Well, well! What's this? A chef carrying a weapon?
Flint: Hold still. Let me have a look at that thing.
Flint: HA! I've spent forty years hammering swords, and nobody ever asked me to forge one of those!
Flint: Anyway, if you're after a Cinderheart Pepper, you'll need to venture into the old forge at Emberfall.
Flint: They built that place around a curious machine. It could turn the mountain's own fire back upon itself.
Flint: They say the furnace doors only opened when the ancient switches were fed the flame they once released.
Flint: Fire's a dangerous thing, chef. But a good piece of metal knows how to send it straight back.
Chef (thought): Maybe this spatula was made for more than cooking.
flint_repeat: Flint: Keep your eyes on the fireballs, not the creature throwing them.
Flint: Timing's everything when you're sending something back where it came from.
quill: Steward Quill: Ah! The chosen chef has arrived!
Steward Quill: His Majesty's feast approaches, and the royal pantry is still missing its most important ingredients.
Steward Quill: Might I suggest a little less sightseeing and a little more gathering?
quill_repeat: Steward Quill: Let me see... Your list is not quite complete.
Steward Quill: Please consult your royal letter. I would rather not serve His Majesty an empty plate.
letter: By royal decree, you have been selected to prepare His Majesty's Birthday Feast! Alas, our royal pantry is terribly unprepared.
Procure three extraordinary treasures: the Dewcrown Mushroom of Riverwood, the Skyfeather Egg of the Whispering Peaks, and the Cinderheart Pepper of Emberfall.
The Village Elder, mountaineer Mira and blacksmith Flint may know the old tales. Return to the Royal Kitchen with all three treasures.
By order of His Royal Majesty — Steward Quill, Keeper of the Royal Kitchens.
Chef: Three ingredients. Three dangerous places. And I've only just had breakfast.
ending: The chef places the three legendary ingredients on the grand kitchen counter.
The mushroom glows softly. The egg shimmers like the morning sky. The pepper radiates a gentle warmth.
Steward Quill: And now, our finest chef, there is only one question left.
Steward Quill: What on earth are you going to cook?
Chef: ...I probably should have thought about that.
